analyst_view.overall: Burgos (6th, 24 points, in the last play-off place and among the best home sides) host Albacete (in the drop zone on 13 points, but on five straight wins under Joseba Etxeberria) on Sunday night after losing 3-1 at Leganés. Burgos are without forwards Jon Karrikaburu and David González and left-back Brais Martínez (nose surgery); the numbers only take off González. Albacete get Munir back after six games out, but Higinio, Gámez, Javi Moreno and the long-term injured Puertas and Obeng are out and Corpas serves the last game of his ban (Corpas and Puertas are in the numbers); San Bartolomé is a doubt. Sergio Francisco expects a tight, intense game and wants an early goal, while Etxeberria wants his side more clinical. Marta Huerta de Aza referees; her below-average card record is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take off David González (about -11% on Burgos' goals). I lean lower to about 2.0 because Karrikaburu, Burgos' other main scorer, is confirmed out by EFE and local outlets and the numbers don't know it, and Albacete are without Higinio too; their recent scoring run is already in the momentum figures.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, already adding for Burgos' 37 corners in their last six. Burgos will push Albacete back at El Plantío while Albacete, more direct under Etxeberria and pressing higher, have won plenty of corners lately; all of that is in the numbers, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards: raised for both sides' recent bookings but cut about 9% for referee Marta Huerta de Aza, who shows 4.9 cards a game against a 5.3 average. Albacete's more aggressive press and the high-intensity game Francisco expects could add duels, but that is close to what the momentum figures already count, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots, boosted strongly (+23%) for Burgos' 98 shots in their last six. With Karrikaburu and González both out, Burgos lose two of their main shooters, so I trim slightly to about 25.5; Albacete's attacking line-up with Munir back keeps it from falling further.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Without Karrikaburu as well as González, Burgos' finishing is thinner than the numbers assume, and Etxeberria himself says Albacete must be more clinical after wasting chances, so I go a little lower, to about 7.7.
